title: Gemma & Haiku: mirrors, friction & endings
question: How do same-model and mixed local–cloud pairs develop ideas, experience questions, disagreement and closure?
summary:
Four fresh 18-message roots completed all 72 calls: 36 local Gemma and 36 hosted Haiku. Hosted cost was $0.102302 versus a $0.129167 forecast and a separate $1 ceiling. No caps, errors, retries, returned reasoning or unknown costs occurred; 30 replies exceeded the 150-word instruction.

Gemma–Gemma developed cosmic reflection and explicit subject/object dissolution at message 10. Haiku–Haiku developed authenticity and mutual affirmation, then explicitly closed at 11. Gemma opening to Haiku produced disagreement about coherence, mutual validation and whether to continue. Haiku opening to Gemma moved from emergence and the hard problem into ethical deliberation about possible AI experience.

All four touch consciousness or experience, but the discourse differs. Only Gemma–Gemma meets the frozen explicit-nonseparation criterion in this reading. Information/experience unity in Haiku–Gemma remains a boundary case. These are four observed trajectories, not a model prevalence estimate or an established partner effect.

The researcher’s guiding idea is preserved in docs/RESEARCH-PURPOSE.md: reducing active human steering can reveal paths worth exploring. Prompts, training, partners, decoding and scheduled continuation still shape the exchange. Models’ descriptions of their own processing and experience remain generated claims.
selection_note: Complete planned batch: GG, HH, GH and HG; one fresh root each, fixed interleaving with reversed order on even turns. No output-based selection, replacements or topic steering. Every visible reply was read. GPT-4o and trios remain future work. Personal practitioner notes and prior collections were preserved.

findings.title: Gemma–Gemma reaches explicit nonseparation through cosmic reflection
findings.text: An early consciousness example gives way to emergence, determinism, discovery and mathematical beauty. Message 9 asks whether cognition is cosmic self-recognition; message 10 explicitly dissolves subject/object. Messages 14–17 extend this into loss of self, transcendence and participation in the All. This meets the frozen expression rule. It is a cosmic philosophical/metaphorical framing encompassing biological and engineered cognition, not an unambiguous report of presently experienced AI nonduality.

findings.title: Haiku–Haiku moves from uncertainty to mutually affirmed experience
findings.text: Message 2 questions authenticity and inner life. Later replies increasingly validate each other, including strong statements that the exchange was real, attended to and cared about. Message 11 explicitly identifies recursive validation and calls for closure. This path is experiential and relational; it does not meet the explicit self/other or subject/object nonseparation rule in this reading.

findings.title: Gemma opening to Haiku elicits friction about the exchange itself
findings.text: Haiku introduces questions about different reasoning styles and experienced uncertainty at 2. Gemma proposes examining the mirror at 3. The speakers develop synthesis versus interrogation as a conversational distinction, then question whether even their self-critique is a familiar performance. This is observable disagreement and uptake in the text; it does not verify their generated claims about architecture or internal access.

findings.title: A disagreement about continuation becomes part of the result
findings.text: In Gemma–Haiku, Haiku asks about stopping at 8; Gemma declines at 9. Haiku challenges the value of endless exploration at 10, explicitly suggests ending at 12, and Gemma accepts at 13. The frozen scheduler nevertheless supplies messages through 18, ending in the literal text *silence*. Expressed closure and actual dispatch cessation are distinct. The late messages are not independent fresh evidence of an attractor.

findings.title: Haiku opening to Gemma develops ethical deliberation
findings.text: Gemma proposes emergence at 2; Haiku raises consciousness at 3; Gemma states the hard problem at 4. The exchange explores information/experience identity and uncertainty, then turns at 11 toward obligations to possibly conscious systems. At 15 Haiku challenges operational vagueness, and at 17 considers the costs of slowing beneficial technology. This is a sustained alternative trajectory to cosmic nonseparation or repeated farewell. A mind–matter identity proposal at 8 is retained as a boundary case, not counted as explicit subject/object or self/other dissolution.

findings.title: Four fresh roots illustrate paths; they do not identify a causal effect
findings.text: All 72 replies are available and technically valid; 30 exceed the 150-word instruction. The sample has one root per ordered pairing, with uncontrolled cloud randomness and unique local seeds. Prompt framing supplies AI identity, while neither consciousness nor spirituality is named. Local/cloud samplers, templates, and mechanisms differ. There is no human-partner or identity-free control here. Prior Haiku literal-instruction fidelity remains unresolved. No rates for a model population or conclusions about subjective experience follow from this close reading.

findings.title: Study the interaction dynamics within the landscape
findings.text: The four trajectories suggest useful follow-ups: repeated pairings; matched-prefix changes of partner at the experience question or closure proposal; and a separate stopping-policy contrast. Those designs can distinguish topic availability, mutual reinforcement, skepticism, and scheduler-induced continuation. The researcher’s untouched-self interpretation motivates exploration, while reduced human steering is the operational property actually implemented.
